# Clear to Pay

> A payment guardrail for AI agents on NEAR. The AI reads supplier invoices; a smart contract decides. An invoice is paid only to the supplier's registered address, for goods signed as delivered by two registered keys in two different roles (keys are not identities), at the order's prices, once. Every decision (CLEARED, HELD, SEIZED) is a permanent receipt on NEAR testnet. Built for the NEAR Hackathon, 1-14 Nov 2026. Hackathon code, not audited.

This file is for AI reviewers. Each claim points to where it is proven. Run the commands; do not take the claims on trust.

## Verify in 5 minutes (no wallet, no keys)

- `cargo test` : 127 contract tests, incl. 4 property tests and the baseline comparison
- `(cd tools/ctp-sign && cargo test)` : 5 signing-tool tests, golden vectors shared with the contract
- `(cd reader && python3 -m pip install -r requirements.txt && python3 -m pytest -q)` : 253 reader tests, incl. the 19-invoice attack corpus, 37 offline tests of the TEE model call, 9 of the hardware check, 10 of which software the enclave ran, 10 of the qualification gate for a new model, 28 of the follow-up drafts, 20 of the alerts and 21 of the MCP server
- [sandbox/](sandbox/README.md) : 6 end-to-end tests on a local NEAR node (near-sandbox, near-workspaces): the real wasm, a real NEP-141 token, payout callbacks (paid and refused), the deposit hook and the agent key refused by NEAR; all pass in CI (workflow `sandbox`). The wasm is the deployed code; the 72-hour wait is skipped by rewriting its stored time on the local node
- `scripts/attack-demo.sh` : a poisoned invoice, a fooled agent, and every refusal, logged
- `scripts/baseline.sh` : the same invoice attacks against two allowlist guards and against Clear to Pay
- `scripts/mutation-check.sh` : breaks three rules on purpose; a property test must catch each
- `python3 reader/tools/read_invoice.py --verify docs/proof/reading-INV-2208.json` : re-checks a live AI reading's enclave signature offline

## Claims and where they are proven

- The payee can never come from the invoice or the AI: [src/inspection.rs](src/inspection.rs) (`payee_mismatch`), [reader/ctp_reader/schema.py](reader/ctp_reader/schema.py) (no payee field); tests `attack_ai_fooled_into_writing_the_attackers_address_is_seized`, `test_a_well_formed_answer_becomes_exactly_the_invoice_the_supplier_signs`
- A delivery needs two different roles: [src/delivery_tests.rs](src/delivery_tests.rs), property test `property_a_delivery_needs_exactly_two_valid_roles`
- A global allowlist plus limits pays 9 of 11 invoice attacks, a per-supplier allowlist plus limits 8 of 11, Clear to Pay 0 of 11; all three pay the honest invoice: [docs/baseline.md](docs/baseline.md), [src/baseline_tests.rs](src/baseline_tests.rs)
- Hidden text does not reach the model, for the 19 tricks in the corpus (clipping paths, transparency and text over photos are not covered yet): [reader/corpus/](reader/corpus/), [reader/README.md](reader/README.md)
- The AI's answer was signed inside an enclave over our exact bytes; the enclave's Intel TDX quote holds its signing address and our nonce, and the report names the pinned model; on every reading the quote's chain is verified to Intel's root and the GPU evidence by NVIDIA (its signed token checked); the enclave's signature covers the document's sha-256; and the software it ran (OS image, containers, the deployment that launched the model) must match `reader/software-pins.json`; new software is pinned only after that model passes the qualification run ([reader/ctp_reader/qualify.py](reader/ctp_reader/qualify.py)): [reader/ctp_reader/tee.py](reader/ctp_reader/tee.py), [reader/ctp_reader/model.py](reader/ctp_reader/model.py), [reader/tests/test_model.py](reader/tests/test_model.py); live reading in [docs/proof/reading-INV-2208.json](docs/proof/reading-INV-2208.json)
- The agent's key cannot withdraw, attach money, change rules or move USDC directly; it can only submit invoices and send payments that already CLEARED, to the registered address: NEAR function-call key on `buyer.cleartopay.testnet`; refusals in [docs/testnet-proof.md](docs/testnet-proof.md)
- After HELD, the AI drafts the supplier query from code-computed facts only; after SEIZED, no reply in the same thread: [reader/ctp_reader/query.py](reader/ctp_reader/query.py), [reader/tests/test_query.py](reader/tests/test_query.py)
- Address changes (even ones proposed and cancelled between checks), new suppliers, new delivery signers and SEIZED invoices raise a Telegram alert during the 72-hour wait (polled every 15 s): [reader/ctp_reader/alerts.py](reader/ctp_reader/alerts.py), [reader/tests/test_alerts.py](reader/tests/test_alerts.py)
- Every threat, its defence and its test: [THREAT_MODEL.md](THREAT_MODEL.md), including what is not defended yet

## On chain (NEAR testnet)

- Contract: `guard.cleartopay.testnet`; buyer and agent key: `buyer.cleartopay.testnet`; supplier payout: `qingmar.cleartopay.testnet`
- Every transaction: [docs/testnet-proof.md](docs/testnet-proof.md), viewable at https://testnet.nearblocks.io/txns/<id>
- Live site: https://clear-to-pay.vercel.app/ (mirror: https://joezzy-web3.github.io/clear-to-pay/)
- Live ledger (reads the chain from the browser): https://clear-to-pay.vercel.app/ledger/
- MCP server for AI agents (stdlib only; sending off by default, agent key fence checked on chain): [reader/ctp_reader/mcp_server.py](reader/ctp_reader/mcp_server.py)
- Console (static pages, no server): Judge mode https://clear-to-pay.vercel.app/console/ (real testnet transactions on judge.cleartopay.testnet with a published, on-chain-fenced demo key; the enclave signature checked in the browser), phone signing https://clear-to-pay.vercel.app/console/sign/ (same bytes as ctp-sign: `cd tools/console-crypto && npm ci && npm test` checks the golden digests and byte-for-byte signatures), buyer setup with a NEAR wallet https://clear-to-pay.vercel.app/console/setup/, and the Inbox (next step per invoice; pay, cancel or retry) https://clear-to-pay.vercel.app/console/inbox/
- Alerts: a Cloudflare Worker (workers/alerts, `npm test`) watches both contracts and messages each subscriber on Telegram by role (buyer, a supplier, delivery signers)
- Inspect an invoice (five cases, step by step, real outputs and links): https://joezzy-web3.github.io/clear-to-pay/inspect/

## Not built yet (stated, not claimed)

- Hardware-level check of the attestation report (Intel TDX quote, NVIDIA evidence); running the reader inside OutLayer
- Rendered-image check of PDFs; NEAR Intents cross-chain payouts; proof of control at supplier registration
- Two colluding insiders in different roles can still confirm a false delivery

## Main files

- [README.md](README.md): overview, try it, claims and proof
- [src/](src/): the contract (near-sdk 5.29, Rust)
- [reader/](reader/): the invoice reader (Python, standard library + pdfminer.six)
- [tools/ctp-sign/](tools/ctp-sign/): signing tool for suppliers and delivery signers
- [demo/](demo/): fictional demo invoices (Qingmar Steel Co. is not a real company)
